# Microsoft Azure Managed Grafana management client library for .NET

Microsoft Azure Managed Grafana is a fully managed service for analytics and monitoring solutions. It's supported by Grafana Enterprise1, which provides extensible data visualizations.

This library supports managing Microsoft Azure Managed Grafana resources.

This library follows the [new Azure SDK guidelines](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/general_introduction.html), and provides many core capabilities:

    - Support MSAL.NET, Azure.Identity is out of box for supporting MSAL.NET.
    - Support [OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io/) for distributed tracing.
    - HTTP pipeline with custom policies.
    - Better error-handling.
    - Support uniform telemetry across all languages.

## Getting started 

### Install the package

Install the Microsoft Azure Managed Grafana management library for .NET with [NuGet](https://www.nuget.org/):

```dotnetcli
dotnet add package Azure.ResourceManager.Grafana
```

### Prerequisites

* You must have an [Microsoft Azure subscription](https://azure.microsoft.com/free/dotnet/).

### Authenticate the Client

To create an authenticated client and start interacting with Microsoft Azure resources, see the [quickstart guide here](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/doc/dev/mgmt_quickstart.md).

## Key concepts

Key concepts of the Microsoft Azure SDK for .NET can be found [here](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/dotnet_introduction.html).

## Documentation

Documentation is available to help you learn how to use this package:

- [Quickstart](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/doc/dev/mgmt_quickstart.md).
- [API References](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/?view=azure-dotnet).
- [Authentication](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/sdk/identity/Azure.Identity/README.md).

## Examples

Code samples for using the management library for .NET can be found in the following locations
- [.NET Management Library Code Samples](https://aka.ms/azuresdk-net-mgmt-samples)

## Troubleshooting

-   File an issue via [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/issues).
-   Check [previous questions](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/azure+.net) or ask new ones on Stack Overflow using Azure and .NET tags.

## Next steps

For more information about Microsoft Azure SDK, see [this website](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/).

## Contributing

For details on contributing to this repository, see the [contributing
guide][cg].

This project welcomes contributions and suggestions. Most contributions
require you to agree to a Contributor License Agreement (CLA) declaring
that you have the right to, and actually do, grant us the rights to use
your contribution. For details, visit <https://cla.microsoft.com>.

When you submit a pull request, a CLA-bot will automatically determine
whether you need to provide a CLA and decorate the PR appropriately
(for example, label, comment). Follow the instructions provided by the
bot. You'll only need to do this action once across all repositories
using our CLA.

This project has adopted the [Microsoft Open Source Code of Conduct][coc]. For
more information, see the [Code of Conduct FAQ][coc_faq] or contact
<opencode@microsoft.com> with any other questions or comments.

decisions.reason: The non-generated factory at lines 33-38 retains a public obsolete, hidden signature but throws unconditionally. The compatibility-shim pattern is appropriate; the original factory it replaces and the motivation for retaining it are not shown.

The handwritten factory overload at lines 44-47 passes the two supplied strings and two null arguments to another overload. A generally generated model-factory overload could plausibly provide this shape; the target overload is outside this capture.

Lines 58-61 explicitly move privateEndpointId from its earlier signature position to the final argument of a delegated factory call. The other overload and its implementation are not supplied, but this handwritten argument-order adapter is independently visible.

Lines 74-78 implement a handwritten output-model factory overload that wraps skuName in ManagedGrafanaSku before delegating. The model-valued overload is not captured, so only this adapter behavior is established.

The handwritten sync and async pageables do yield exactly one page with no continuation, but the catalog's next-link-handling name suggests next-link processing that these implementations do not perform. Use a reusable single-page-pageable pattern instead; the supplied code does not establish whether the service ever returns additional pages.

finding.subtype: Resource action adapted to one-page synchronous and asynchronous pageables
finding.explanation: The resource methods construct sync and async pageables using names from the resource ID and a cancellation-bearing RequestContext. Each AsPages issues one request, projects the response's Value into a page, and supplies a null continuation token. The shown page fetch methods do not use their page-size or continuation-token arguments.
finding.handwrittenRationale: The public resource adapters and both concrete page-fetch and page-projection implementations are present in src/Customization outside Generated.

decisions.reason: Line 16 shows an explicit ResourceData base on the handwritten partial, but no generated counterpart or prior inheritance is supplied. A partial declaration of a base alone does not demonstrate that inheritance was changed or extended relative to the generated API; the proposed override pattern and generator-addressability judgment are therefore unproven.
The handwritten, hidden constructor explicitly initializes two distinct ChangeTrackingList<string> instances at lines 19-24. This is a concrete model-default behavior, not an empty partial.

Lines 26-27 declare a hidden, public get-only IReadOnlyList<string> member in a non-generated partial. The pattern catalog includes added model properties; the claim correctly stops short of asserting that the underlying list is immutable.
Lines 29-30 declare a hidden, public get-only IList<string> member in a non-generated partial. The declared collection interface permits mutation without implying the property itself has a setter.

Lines 14-28 show the handwritten alias getter and both setter branches: create a SKU when absent or update its Name when present. Its public surface is hidden from IntelliSense; serialization and any compatibility motive are not evidenced.

The Customization partial declares an obsolete, IntelliSense-hidden public SMTP property at lines 18-20. Deprecation and retained model surface are visible; no serialization or wire mapping is claimed.

The separate ManagedGrafanaProperties partial independently declares the obsolete, hidden SMTP property at lines 18-20. This is a distinct model member from the patch-properties member; wire behavior is not established.

The handwritten hidden sync and async overloads at lines 87-103 invoke Update with WaitUntil.Completed and await or call WaitForCompletion to return resource responses. They adapt public method signatures and results, not the underlying LRO poller.

The patch model's handwritten SkuName accessors at lines 13-27 mirror the data-model alias but modify a different public model. The two setter branches are explicit; the service's wire representation is not shown.

The non-generated Smtp partial is obsolete and hidden, and the cited lines establish a constructor-assigned model state and public SMTP settings. Its empty public constructor is not a standalone customization; the grouped handwritten public settings model is. No transport, JSON serialization, or historical provenance is inferred.

The non-generated value type at lines 15-55 defines the named string values, conversion, case-insensitive equality and matching hash, and stored-string representation. These are value-model behaviors; this capture shows no TLS negotiation.

omissions.subtype: Diagnostic scope around synchronous and asynchronous pageable fetches
omissions.explanation: Both handwritten page-fetch implementations start a named ClientDiagnostics scope before invoking the pipeline and record an exception on that scope before rethrowing it. Whether this instrumentation merits a separate counted instance rather than being grouped with the same page-fetch methods' pagination behavior needs independent assessment.
omissions.handwrittenRationale: The explicit scope start and failure handling are implemented in both Customization/CollectionResults pageables outside Generated; the scope is not merely mentioned in a comment.
